extracted.intended_audience: investigators applying for the NIH Director's Pioneer Award (DP1)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and review criteria for preparing and submitting an application to the NIH Director's Pioneer Award (DP1 Clinical Trial Optional), emphasizing highly innovative, high-risk/high-reward projects and substantial changes in research direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications need not be strong in every scored criterion to have major scientific impact; reviewers consider all scored and additional criteria when assigning the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion of the aims change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For clinical trials: evaluate the scientific rationale, necessity of the trial for testing hypotheses or interventions, whether trial addresses important questions or unmet needs, and whether results could change clinical practice or lead to new scientific avenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD(s)/PI(s), collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? Do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated ongoing accomplishments that advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider appropriateness of leadership, complementary expertise, governance and organizational structure. For clinical trials, assess expertise in study coordination, data management, statistics, and whether organizational structure fits a multicenter trial and meeting enrollment, protocol adherence, and data collection needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge existing paradigms, employ novel concepts, approaches or methodologies, or address an innovative direction? Applications should reflect substantially different scientific directions and may involve exceptionally innovative approaches or radically unconventional hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be considered pioneering, the proposed research must reflect substantially different scientific directions from those already being pursued by the investigator or elsewhere and cannot be an obvious extension or scale-up of current research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will evaluate the feasibility, rigor, and overall strategy for accomplishing the proposed research. Although Pioneer applications do not require detailed experimental plans or extensive preliminary data, reviewers must have a clear sense of the overall research and be convinced that it will be pursued robustly and rigorously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Research Strategy should not present a detailed plan, but should describe pioneering approaches and how the work will be pursued; applicants are recommended to state that detailed plans/preliminary data are not being provided per NOFO. Flexibility to pivot during the award is expected given the high-risk nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment contribute to the probability of success? Are institutional support, equipment and other physical resources adequate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements enhance likelihood of success. For clinical trials, assess appropriateness of administrative, data coordinating, enrollment and laboratory/testing centers and site capability for trial conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline (clinical trials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the study timeline described in detail, accounting for start-up activities, anticipated enrollment rate, and planned follow-up? Is the projected timeline feasible and well justified?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for feasibility, plans to address challenges (e.g., enrollment shortfalls), and use of efficiencies/resources (CTSAs, registries, EMRs) to increase enrollment and data collection efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, evaluate: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For exempt research, evaluate justification for exemption, human subjects involvement and characteristics, and sources of materials. Refer to NIH Guidelines for Review of Human Subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Human Subjects Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: When projects involve human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, reviewers will evaluate the proposed plans for inclusion of relevant populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NIH Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research when assessing inclusivity plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals using: (1) complete description of procedures including species, strains, ages, sex, and total numbers; (2) justification that the species is appropriate and why alternatives cannot be used; and (3) interventions (analgesia, anesthesia, humane endpoints) to limit pain/distress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods of euthanasia and justification if not consistent with AVMA guidelines are required. Refer to Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animals Section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether proposed materials or procedures are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards exist, reviewers will determine whether adequate protections are proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess information provided on Select Agent(s) including: which agents will be used, registration status of entities, procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer, and plans for biosafety, biocontainment, and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable when Select Agents are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the Resource Sharing Plan(s) or the rationale for not sharing resources is reasonable (e.g., Sharing Model Organisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are provided but Resource Sharing Plans do not receive separate scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects involving key biological and/or chemical resources, reviewers will comment on plans for identifying and ensuring the validity of those resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers provide commentary on the brief plans proposed for authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget justification is assessed but not given a separate score; ensure requested Direct Costs align with NOFO ($700,000 per year direct costs; $3,500,000 total for 5 years entered in SF424 fields). Detailed budgets and standard R&R budgets are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy Essay Structure and Content (Application formatting requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Strategy must be structured as an essay, uploaded as a PDF named 'Essay.pdf', and must contain sections in the order given with headings: Scientific Areas; Project Title; Project description; Evidence of PD's/PI's innovativeness; How the planned research substantially differs from the PD's/PI's past or current work; Suitability for Pioneer Award program; Statement of research effort commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe innovative vision, importance, qualifications, and avoid detailed experimental plans or extensive preliminary data. Include science area codes and project title at top; lists of collaborators’ names/affiliations may be included but letters of collaboration will not be accepted. Figures/illustrations may be included but must fit within page limits. References are not required but, if included, must fit within page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Reference (requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs must arrange for three (and only three) confidential letters of reference to be submitted electronically; missing letters render an application incomplete and it will not be reviewed. Late letters will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters: up to two pages; describe PD/PI qualities supporting innovativeness with specific examples and likelihood of conducting groundbreaking research. Letters submitted previously will not be retrieved; referees submit at the specified Commons URL without signing in. The PD/PI must provide referees with PD/PI Commons User ID and exact name as in Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Effort Commitment (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pioneer recipients are required to commit the major portion of their research effort (more than 6 person-months or at least 51%) to activities supported by the Pioneer Award in the first three years; effort may be reduced to a minimum of 4 person-months (33%) in year four and 3 person-months (25%) in year five.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with current commitments equal to 6 person-months or more must explain how effort on existing grants will be adjusted to meet Pioneer Award requirements. Investigators unable to meet these requirements should not submit applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial Change in Research Direction / Novelty Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered pioneering, the proposed research must reflect substantially different ideas from those being pursued in the investigator's current research program or elsewhere and cannot be an obvious extension or scale-up of a current research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed project must represent a new and distinct direction motivated by a fundamental new insight; applications that are straightforward extensions of ongoing research should not be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single PD/PI and Restrictions on Senior/Key Personnel & Attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Only single PD/PI applications are allowed. Only the PD/PI may serve as senior/key personnel and only the PD/PI may submit a Biographical Sketch. Information on collaborators may be included in the Essay, but letters of collaboration and collaborator biosketches will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use profile fields for additional senior/key persons, additional biographical sketches, or R&R Budget; follow NOFO-specific 'DO NOT USE' instructions for many standard forms/attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Limitations and Appendix Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All page limitations described in the How to Apply – Application Guide and the Table of Page Limits must be followed. The Appendix is limited: no publications or other materials may be included except blank questionnaires or blank surveys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and illustrations may be included in the Essay but must fit within the page limits. References, if included, must fit within page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Routing Identifier / Science Area Designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate the two most appropriate scientific areas (primary and secondary) using the one-digit code and abbreviation (e.g., '1 BSS') and enter them in Agency Routing Identifier (Field 4b) and at the beginning of the Research Strategy essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose two science areas most appropriate for the project to aid assignment to reviewers; science area designations do not affect funding potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Submission Requirements & Registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organizations must complete and maintain required registrations prior to submission: SAM (with UEI), NCAGE for foreign orgs, eRA Commons, and Grants.gov. PD(s)/PI(s) must have eRA Commons accounts. Applications must be submitted electronically via Grants.gov and tracked in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrations can take 6 weeks or more; failure to complete registrations is not a valid reason for late submission. Include PD/PI Commons ID in credential field. Follow 'How to Apply - Application Guide' for full instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Completeness, Compliance, and Responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt, applications will be evaluated for completeness and compliance with application instructions by CSR and responsiveness by the Office of Strategic Coordination. Applications that are incomplete, non-compliant and/or nonresponsive will not be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are responsible for monitoring submission status and correcting errors prior to the due date. Follow 'Dealing with System Issues' guidance if system problems threaten on-time submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Submission Materials Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are required to follow NIH instructions for post-submission materials; for this NOFO, only documents informing of unforeseen events (e.g., natural disasters) that substantially affect ability to execute proposed research will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other post-submission information is generally not accepted; follow linked policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must address a Data Management and Sharing Plan consistent with NIH policy. For this NOFO, Resource Sharing Plans are expected as Just-in-Time information if an award is being considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data management/sharing is applicable, recipients must implement the approved plan upon award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Specific Requirements and IC Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators proposing NIH-defined clinical trials are advised to consult relevant NIH Institutes/Centers to ensure conformance to IC clinical trial research policies. Funding is contingent on conformance to the administering IC's policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical trial applications should refer to Research Methods Resources for design/statistics and include appropriate PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information records as instructed in the How to Apply guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Cost Sharing Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: This NOFO does not require cost sharing as defined in the NIH Grants Policy Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not plan on cost sharing to meet eligibility or review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview Stage and Selection Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates identified as the most outstanding after initial review will be invited for interviews (March–April 2026) conducted by a panel of external experts; the same review criteria will be used during interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final funding decisions will consider peer review merit, availability of funds, conformance to IC policies, portfolio balance, and program priorities (potential for investigator to lead groundbreaking research, cross-cutting science, national impact).
